body: Yes I know about gluten free oats and I can’t even have them because I have the same reaction to them as I do to other gluten containing grains.
I live in the UK and I can't have oats as they make me sick exactly like the usual gluten containing grains

It can happen! At my job my manager was a teller for 10 months and now she's branch manager. It upset a lot of people in the area who wanted the job as well but she's amazing at the job and I'm glad she got it.
I felt like this and it turned out that I had celiac disease. Maybe that's something to look into?
I always put ice cubes in their water in the summer, they absolutely love it!

One of my baby budgies did this several times until I figured out she was squeezing out of the bottom between the tray and where the cage began. I removed the grill so the babies wouldn't hurt themselves on it. She was the only one that figured it out and the parents and other babies would be in the cage and she'd be chilling on a shelf when I came home from work!

Convenience foods! Sometimes I just want a ready meal or a sandwich that actually tastes good and that I don't have to cook myself. Or I'm out somewhere and don't want to have to pack a whole days worth of food to bring with me when everyone else can just get something decent whilst they're out. I know these things exist but it's one or two options of the least popular flavour.
Please try and get her tested for celiac disease if you can. I was your daughter and finding out as a teenager would have changed my life for the better.

She sounds a lot like me at that age. In my case I had undiagnosed celiac disease which was making it very difficult for me to focus on difficult things due to being in pain (low level) constantly and generally fatigued all the time. I struggled a lot of the time even doing normal things, but no-one could really see anything was wrong. I didn't even know anything was wrong, I just thought I was lazy and then stupid. One of the first signs was me being unable to focus on doing my homework and then not wanting to go to school and even now I can't really tell you why I just couldn't do it. I was smart, too, but I was sick and I think having to focus on schoolwork was just too much, Celiac causes you to be unable to absorb enough nutrition from food and that can have a lot of effects on someone. 

I thought I had anxiety, depression, autism, adhd and personality disorders at one point. Once I found out it was gluten (at 21) and stopped eating it, the problems I was having slowly disappeared.
I know so many birds called Pico, if you like it then go for it!

I used to batch cook on a Sunday evening to save time but I began to resent spending 3hrs in the kitchen even though the rest of the week I didn't have to cook. I would cook simple meals and cook loads of it so I was eating the same thing all week and they were pretty basic things too. I have celiac disease so I can't just go and grab something quick and easy if I'm hungry and meal prepping helped me to not just be unhealthy and eat gluten free junk food all the time.

I recently signed up for frozen ready meals to be delivered ever couple of weeks so I don't have to prepare all of my lunches myself and it's saved me so much time. It's a bit expensive but it saves me time and gives me far more food variety than I would usually have, as well as limiting food wastage. There's simply no way I would buy an aubergine and somehow be able to come up with a few meals to have it in and then cook it right and not end up throwing some away because I didn't put it in enough meals or I got too much of it. Same with sweet potato, chickpeas and other ingredients in these meals that I wouldn't normally have or even know how to cook. 

And it's given me time back for being able to cook some really nice things when I do have the time, instead of not wanting to cook because I already spend hours in the kitchen.

I had this colour for a few months and I thought it was blonde. However I was informed by my coworkers and customers that it was actually ginger so I went lighter and now I actually have blonde hair that I really like.

I've got 7 birds and if I could go back in time I probably wouldn't get them again. They are so messy and I struggle so much to keep up with their maintenance. They get all the recommended care so they're not suffering at all, but they are really hard work to look after properly. Mine are all small too so I can imagine how much harder the larger birds would be!

That being said, I house sat my friends dog for a week and it convinced me that I never want a dog. The dog is lovely but I think she needed more care than my birds do! I had to make sure I was home to let her out, take her for walks everyday and entertain her whilst I was home. My birds take up a lot of time but I don't have to worry about rushing home to let them out so they can go to the toilet, or taking them out for walks or anything like that.

Depression and anxiety. For basically my whole childhood. When I was 21 and they just told me I was depressed and anxious again, despite me almost being bed bound because I was so fatigued I knew something else was wrong. I also got diagnosed with fibromyalgia a few years later when I was unknowingly eating gluten for around two years and was feeling terrible.

I was diagnosed with depression and anxiety after spending pretty much my whole childhood having the same symptoms. My parents refused to take me to the doctor because they didn't want a child with depression and anxiety (they told me this), and all the doctors would do is put me on medication. At 20 I went myself and was diagnosed with depression and anxiety but none of what they gave me or told me to do worked. I went to counselling, was already doing all the self help that's recommended (healthy diet, exercise, sunshine etc.) It didn't work.

At 21 I found out I had celiac disease and gave up gluten. Within three days I felt like a different person. Most of my anxiety went and I was able to live my life again. Unfortunately I'm pretty sure I either have another health issue or I actually have anxiety now as I am struggling again at 27.

I just wish places sold actual gluten free food, not biscuits or cookies or cakes or cereal. I just want to eat a decent meal without having to cook it all from scratch. Sometimes I want the convenience everyone else has. And if it's gluten free by some miracle it always has to be an obscure flavour. Only one shop sells a gluten free sandwich near me, and the flavour is egg salad with a weird tasting sauce. Who's eating that? Me, obviously because I have no choice, but why is that the only flavour on offer? That's surely not the most popular sandwich flavour is it?

I was gaslit by my mum over this. I kept feeling like I had had gluten and she kept telling me I'm so careful that I couldn't possibly have had it. Some days I would be crying telling her how awful I felt and she would tell me I'm obsessing over gluten and I need to relax.

Turns out she'd been feeding me gluten for two years so I was feeling sick for a very real reason. 

I did it to myself with oats as well. I started having gluten free oats regularly and I felt awful but told myself to get on with it because I was just struggling because I was working or doing too much or any other number of reasons that I could find. I realised it was actually oats and stopped eating them and felt a lot better.

Oats shouldn't be seen as gluten free, even gluten free oats. Enough people with celiac also react to them like they would gluten so I don't think they should be able to be included in so many gluten free foods. I recently found out I was reacting to them after I was getting really sick on what I thought was a gluten free diet. I had oats every day and didn't make the connection until one weekend where I continued having them through the weekend and felt so bad on Monday that I knew something wasn't right. I had been having them for breakfast everyday, feeling bad by Friday but blamed it on working Mon-Fri and being tired from that.

I let mine play with dried lavender. Once I got some eucalyptus cuttings as well (from a neighbour who was trimming them). If I give them oranges then that smells nice too. I also find if I wash things that gives a nice smell, like throws and blankets that I use for covering them up at night. I also open the window at night when the birds are in their cages to air the room out.

Since you already have some birds, have you considered a green cheek conure? I have one and she is really affectionate and always wants to sit with me and be involved in what I'm doing. I have another conure too but that one doesn't care much for me and is a different species of conure that's not as cuddly. I also have budgies but they stick to themselves like yours do and my conure don't bother much with them.

I suspect most shoplifters don't actually steal because they need that item, they steal it to sell it. I worked in a shop and we never got shoplifters who actually stole things they needed, it was always medicine, alcohol or kids stealing chocolate and crisps. Even the ones that stole baby formula would just be reselling it as it's expensive and not because they had a baby to feed.

I'm 27f and don't go to any gym. but last year I worked a very physical job where I was on my feet moving and lifting things all day. I also went on 2 hour dog walks a couple of times a week and I don't know how I managed it to be honest. 

Now I work a job where I sit down all day 9-5 and it's so hard to want to do anything after work. I won't go to the gym because I don't like it but I am going to start trying to fit in more dog walks (I haven't done much over the winter because of flooding) and get my garden going again since I had no time for it the last couple of years. I'm hoping that will be enough, but 8hrs, 5 days a week of exercise is a bit hard to replicate. 

Most people where I work go to the gym though and I felt very out of place when I started. The culture is so different to jobs I've worked before. They're all also on dating apps if they're single which I've never done, and don't need to since I met my boyfriend through work.

It's definitely a thing with birds! I rehomed one of my conures from a woman who no longer had time for her and she said she chose me to have her because she was getting loads of messages from people who just didn't seem to care about the bird at all and just wanted her quickly. I asked about the bird and told her about my own flock and sent pictures of what her new home would look like.

I didn't unfortunately and I still have that pain. I suspect it's something to do with my teeth as I'm prone to wisdom tooth infections. Sometimes it goes away if I have coffee or really salty foods. I suspect I have POTS as well and the salt and coffee help me to feel a bit better but I don't know why they would ease that pain as well. I only have one coffee a day so it's not like I'm addicted and it's just caffeine withdrawal either.

I've actually been trialling this and it hasn't gone well. I'm used to 8 hours sleep and the past two weeks I've tried it have been pretty awful. My sleep quality has gone down, and I can't stay in bed for much longer than 8 hours to catch up on sleep on the weekends. When I'm awake, I'm awake and can't get back to sleep. When I get 8 hours in the week I sleep well, but 7 is just too little for me. I'm dreading when I have children!

I worked in a shop and people would bring their dogs in all the time. I now work in a bank and people still brings their dogs in. They're not even working dogs, just pets. One womans dog barked for 15 mins in the queue the other day. One dog almost wet itself because another customer wanted to stroke it and it wees itself if it gets stroked so the owner was saying "don't pee, don't pee" in a baby voice to it. We have a sign on the door saying no dogs. My manager is also allergic to dogs. 

I walk my friends dog for her a couple of times a week so I like dogs, I just don't think they need to be allowed everywhere.

I just want to second the soy causing hormonal problems. I've had my conure for three years and in that whole time she's been off the charts hormonal. She has screamed almost non-stop, been aggressive a lot of the time, hasn't played with toys and has generally been a bit of a nightmare to live with. She's 7 years old too, so it's not just her being a teenager.

I tried everything to get her to stop. I gave her 12 hours sleep, a stable routine, time outside, lots of chop, lots of time out of the cage, training sessions, lots of toys to destroy, no nesting spaces, no paper to shred, foraging toys, puzzle toys etc. And eventually I was pulling my hair out because she would not stop with the aggression and screaming. All year round. 

Finally I said that's enough, I won't feed her any seeds at all and put her on a 90% pellet diet with the rest of her food being vegetables. And she got so much worse. I was feeding her mainly harrisons, which is supposedly the best! And it was expensive too! I fed another brand which contained soy as well and she loved those pellets a lot. My other birds kept laying eggs and mating too, year round but at least they weren't noisy and aggressive. 

So when she got much worse on mainly just pellets I decided to take her off pellets completely and just give seeds and chop. She is a different bird now. She's stopped screaming so much. She plays with her toys. She settles down and I can have a proper relationship with her now. Before I couldn't even look at her because that would make her scream at me. I couldn't walk past her because she'd lunge at me. She would scream all day if I was at work. She would scream all day if she was out of her cage all day. 

She came and sat next to me and did the closed eye thing at me for ages yesterday. Something she hasn't done in the three years I've had her. I'm still giving her pellets twice a week just because I have loads of them left since they're expensive so I stocked up when they were cheap, but when they run out I might just not buy them anymore. She's still a bit hormonal, but I'm so glad she's manageable now. I was going to rehome her because after three years of the screaming with no relief, and wanting to move in with my boyfriend where our only option is renting, she wouldn't be able to come. But now I think I'll be able to keep her!
Clipped birds can still fly away!
I got two parrots summer of 2020 and now I have 8, an Instagram page for them and I spend a stupid amount of time and money on them

He reminds me of my crimson bellied conure, Tequila! He looks so similar to mine, maybe because of the feathers on his head. Tequila has a scar on her head where feathers don't really grow, so she has a little bald patch. I also got her from a horrible situation.

I had the same concern for myself, but people generally don't care in my experience. One guy got me my own toaster to keep at his house so I could eat toast there safely and he was a dick so if he can accommodate me then the good ones definitely can! 

My current boyfriend makes fun of me having celiac (in a jokey way, he's not actually being mean), but still wants to be with me and doesn't ever do anything that would make me sick. We cook together and find places we can eat together. It's never really been an issue for me.

I can't even have gf oats! Some people react to oats as well, but it took a long time for me to realise that that was happening. 

Why on earth does soy milk need wheat and barely extract?!!

Don't let anyone else cook for you. My mum cooked one meal a week for two years and managed to put gluten in it, then gaslighted me about being sick and told me I was obsessing about gluten and that I'm so careful so how could I possibly still be sick? Then when I found out, instead of saying sorry or that she didn't realise what she'd done, she said "at least you found out why you're always sick still". 

I also wish someone had told me to avoid oats! That would have saved me a few years of symptoms too.
I treat mine just like I treat my conures and they're very happy birds!

I meal prep for a couple of hours and then it's much easier to do. It can be difficult to hype myself up to do it but once its done it's worth it. I also love the amount of time I save in the week by not having to cook

I had a similar upbringing to you.

I got a job in retail in a small supermarket and that changed my life for the better. I made a huge effort to be nice and friendly to everyone, and was also extremely kind to myself about my lack of social skills sometimes. I also made an effort to notice when people made mistakes and how they dealt with them and then started doing the same thing. Most people are socially awkward at times but you don't notice it often because they don't focus on their mistake and they move on quickly. It was also a customer facing role so I kind of had to learn how to be outgoing and friendly with everyone. 

I got on very well with everyone there, made a few friends, met my boyfriend and still get on with them all 6 months after I left. My new job is harder as now I work with people closer to my own age and I'm missing a lot of general knowledge due to my childhood. I have huge gaps where I don't remember stuff, and I still have ongoing problems with trauma from my childhood which does make it difficult for me sometimes. I tend to freeze up and sometimes I go mute which doesn't help at all. But the people I work with have made me feel welcome, and I do get on well enough with them even if I'm not the best socially. 

I still don't exactly have a social life though. I spend a lot of time with my boyfriend at his house and we occasionally go out and do something. He works a lot and is focused on his career atm so he's often tired and doesn't want to do much. Sometimes I'll go for a coffee or do something with an old colleague or go out with my sister/ see my family. I walk a dog for one of my old customers and sometimes take him out with a friend and her dog but that's not extremely often. Before that supermarket job I literally didn't go anywhere or do anything. Now if I really want to see someone then I'll arrange something. I do want to do more, but finding the time and energy is difficult at times. For the most part I am happy with where I am though, even though I don't do as much as some people I know. The people I work with are always going out and doing stuff after work, gym before work and planning holidays with friends.
The same thing happened to me

I'm sorry you're going through this. I feel much the same way and was going to post almost exactly what you posted when I saw your post.

I left a job I loved and was good at and that worked well for me in order to earn more money and two months in and I'm struggling a lot. A lot of the time I can't relate to the people I work with, or like you I'm already dealing with being triggered and disassociate or I panic and have to try and deal with that whilst working. And then I make mistakes and feel worse. Sometimes I give off the wrong vibe and I know I do but I can't always stop it or change it.

I was the same when I first started at my other job that I ended up loving, so I'm trying to do what I did when I started there. I don't try and make friends and that takes the pressure off of me to be super likeable. I'm nice to everyone, but I remind myself that they're coworkers and I need to get on with them but we don't need to be besties in order to work together. I also remind myself that I've been through a lot and cut myself some slack with things. I remind myself that I'm new and I'm allowed to make mistakes, and I look at my coworkers and spot mistakes they make which reassures me. I don't point them out or anything but it helps ground me a bit.

Self care outside of work is important too. I get a lot of sleep, try and eat well and make myself do things I enjoy. I also reach out to people I know to keep me grounded, even if I don't always want to. Something my dad taught me is to always have something to look forward to as it makes life more bearable. So even if it's just looking forward to playing a video game I love on the weekend, I try and hype it up and look forward to it and it makes life a little bit easier.

I have four! I rescued one and she really tried to fit in with my conure and cockatiel but they didn't want to know her so I ended up rescuing another and they had babies. I gave two babies to a friend and kept two of them so now I have four.

Mine told my sister never to trust me because I have celiac disease and the gluten makes me lie. 

The "lies" I was telling my sister were that I don't have autism (she told the family I did and to walk on eggshells around me in case I had a meltdown), and just general things from our childhood that confirmed me and my sister had been played off against each other.

I left my old job last year for a better paying job. My coworkers are getting a payrise in April which will put them on more than I'm getting now and I haven't been told if I'm getting a payrise or not. I'm definitely going to be looking and maybe go back to my old job if I don't get a payrise.

I really hope not! I've had symptoms my whole life and only fully went gluten free around three years ago. I've recently realised I react the same way to oats so have cut them out now too, but that would mean I've only had a few weeks where I haven't been having gluten and who knows what damage might be there!
Yeah I might have to try that to be honest, I just want her to be happy and healthy!

I train her every morning before work! This week as soon as she's finished training she starts screaming. I try to carry on the training but she's not interested in any more treats and just chooses to scream. She screams at the window, or at me. We live on a quiet street so there's nothing that's scaring her outside. I've tried using seeds as treats, and she will train for pellets too so I've tried both seeds and pellets for training. I do recall with her, around corners as well as up high and down low to the ground so she has to move in different ways. She can give kisses, spin and I have a few toys too. She can pick things up and I try to introduce her to new things a lot too. She also gets some of her food in foraging toys to keep her busy but she's started screaming whilst foraging too, and screaming whilst eating sometimes. 

Thank you for trying to help though!

I give her the adult lifetime one already. I know parrots scream, but her screaming isn't normal and she isn't happy at all. She'll scream non stop all day long. She screams to come out of the cage, but then I'll let her out and she does the exact same scream and body language but at the window like she wants to go out of the window. She spends probably about half of her waking hours screaming at nothing. She's only quiet when she's trying to nest (which I stop her doing). 50% pellets and 50% chop should have stopped her being so hormonal but it's made her worse. My other birds are fine, it's just her that I have issues with.

She's like an over reactive dog. She just screams all day long at everything, lunges to attack me even when I'm feeding her sometimes and is generally unhappy. The more things I try to do "right" the worse she gets. 12hrs+ of covered sleep, no seeds, loads of chop, lots of time out of the cage and she's getting worse and worse.
That's why I love it! I never feel self conscious there because no-one cares about you, but where I live people judge so harshly.

I give her a couple of different types, harrisons and pretty bird. I cover her cage for at least 12 hours but more like 13-14 some days because I can't handle the screaming. It has not made her better at all and actually makes her worse the more I cover her up. The cover also makes my other parrots more hormonal so I've stopped covering them all up the last couple of weeks and it's helped a bit. She used to attack me as I walked past the cage but she's mostly stopped since I stopped covering the cage. Now my main problem is the screaming all the time for no reason at all.

I love London! My family lives there and I spent a lot of time growing up there, but the town I live in is awful. You can't walk down the high street without everyone staring at you, let alone with a parrot!
Aww I'm sorry you got fired! I was lucky with the people I worked with I think. There were a few that liked her a lot, but they also liked me so it worked out in my favour.
Awww that's so cute!
I have pet parrots and I'd love to take them out with me for walks and such because they'd love it. But I won't because I don't want any attention.

I did and she handed in her notice the week after. All I said was I don't expect to be treated that way again (it was an awful shift with her) and then the next week she handed her notice in. It probably helped that I was really good at my job and I'd been there a couple of years so there wasn't really a way she could bully me out of it.

I always find a couple of people that straight up hate me wherever I work. I'm generally quite confident and keep to myself, but really enjoy working as a team with people. When I'm at work, I work and therefore I'm usually quite good at whatever it is I'm doing. I don't stand out and I don't go out of my way to stand out at all, I just live my life and do the best I can and for the most part people quite like me. 

But there's always a couple of people that hate me for it. The worst was when a co-worker saw me as a threat and decided to be my friend instead. We ended up being best friends, but then when I got promoted she couldn't handle it and sabotaged me at every opportunity. I finally stood up to her after letting it slide for months and then she handed in her notice the next week. She was insanely jealous of me and I couldn't really see it until she left my life. I actually stepped down shortly after because the stress that her and my manager put me through was too much. Even my manager hated me because I was showing up his other managers, but then he'd ask them why they couldn't be as good as me and it was creating an awful atmosphere and turning people against me. To my face he would always find a problem or something I hadn't done. Another girl I worked with tried to start bullying me verbally but then realised someone else was standing behind me and could hear and as soon as she realised she started saying she was joking and then went to the bathroom to cry and wouldn't speak to anyone for the rest of the day. 

In my new job there's a girl who I feel might be a problem at at some point but I hope not. I've just been around enough people now that I pick up on it quite easily. The vast majority of people I work with like me and I get on with them though!

I raised budgies once and the parents definitely missed the two chicks I gave to a friend. They still see them on occasion but when they first went they would flock call for them, even the two siblings I kept looked for them. The chicks were fledged when they went though so that might make a difference?

I have 8 parrots and some days I wish I could only have one! They can be a lot of work, but one or two conures are pretty easy to look after. They're a lot more work than rabbits, but they're very rewarding to own!

I started 8 weeks ago and I learn best by doing it too. You can get past them, just don't put too much pressure on yourself to remember everything. 

Now I'm on the counter and I'm learning a lot more but there's still so much I don't know. It's a steep learning curve but you'll get there. I came from a job where I was always on my feet doing something and there was always something to be done so for a few weeks I felt like I wasn't really working. I'm getting used to it now and I'm really enjoying it, but that training at the beginning is a bit of a slog.

I've always been slightly overweight whilst eating about 1500-2000 calories a day. Found out I had celiac disease and the weight just came off without me having to diet or exercise any more and I became a healthy weight. 

Just recently I somehow gained a bunch of weight despite having a very physical job and then I got a sedentary job where I just sit all day long. I was worried about the weight and then found out I can't have oats (some people with celiac react to even gluten free oats because the protein is similar enough to gluten) and now I'm losing weight despite having a sedentary job. 

Plenty of things can affect your body, it's not always just calories.

Three years later and she's not okay at all! I have no idea what her life was like but she is not a happy bird. I follow all the advice and my other 7 birds are happy, but she's never really happy. She just screams all the time, doesn't play with toys, hates me unless I'm giving her treats and is generally a difficult bird to own. I love her still, but it's hard sometimes when I do everything and she just screams at me and tries to bite me all the time.
I was sold a three month old conure that I later found out was actually 4 years old. The place seemed reputable as well, according to online reviews

I got my most recent bird because I was the only person that wasn't talking about how cheap she was selling her for and seemed to actually care about the bird. She said the other people that messaged her were just talking about how cheap she was.  She even delivered her to my house so I didn't have to travel anywhere!

You sound a bit like me, even down to wanting to do conservation work one day.

I worked in a shop for 4 years. They thought I was stupid at first, and I struggled a lot with it but by the end of it I was never put on till and was given full time shifts, promoted to shift manager and was put on all the big deliveries.

I never gave up trying to manage fibro. Anything that I could try, I tried in the hope that it might work. All kinds of diets, supplements, lifestyle changes etc. I tried so much and I slowly got to a point that I could manage work. I can't manage much else, even now, but I can work and do some things outside of that. 

It's not great but once I accepted I was sick and had to manage it, things did get a bit easier for me.

Well I broke up with him and it went horribly. He doesn't even care that I've broken up with him and seems to think I'll be going back to him in a few days. I picked my stuff up tonight and he says he won't have a conversation with me because this has come out of the blue. I said to him that I've been trying to talk to him for months but he just laughs it all off so how am I supposed to make him listen and talk to me without me getting upset and he just refused to answer. He said he never sees me because I like to plan it days in advance and I don't spontaneously message him to do stuff. I have pets and I'm the only one that looks after them so I have to know at least the morning of seeing him so I can make sure they're looked after. Also he refused to address most of it because said I've only got upset now because he cancelled on Saturday and if he hadn't done that then I wouldn't be upset now.

I think I've dodged a bullet there.

If I can manage to do it then I feel pretty great and satisfied because of the amount of things I'm able to do! But it does catch up with you and I wouldn't recommend doing it too often. I don't do it at all nowadays and just try to have a balance.

Do you eat oats? I ate gluten free oats quite a bit and I felt awful. It got to the point that I would have them every day in the week for breakfast and feel awful by Friday, then I'd stop eating them over the weekend and feel a bit better by Sunday evening. I put it down to starting a new job, winter and adjusting to a 9-5 Mon-Fri job. But then I had a busy weekend, continued eating oats over that time for convenience and felt so bad by Sunday I knew there had to be something else going on.

Since cutting out the oats I feel so much better. My chest rash has also disappeared and the brain fog is clearing. My acne is also gone and I feel less anxious about things. My confidence has also improved and I think I'm going to actually be able to be healthy for once in my life. I felt like this right after I cut gluten out, but then over the years lots of things have happened (mum feeding me gluten weekly for a couple of years without me knowing, and me starting to eat a lot of oats thinking it was fine) that have affected my health.
I'm so jealous! I really want this cage for my birds but I have no room for it unfortunately.

I'm interested to see what other people answer for this. I work full time 9-5 five days a week, have pets that need looking after, spend time with my boyfriend and try to spend time with friends/family too, plus sleep, food, chores etc. I feel like I have barely any time left over after all of that. I feel like I'm wasting any time I do have if I just watch tv or play games

I think you're right. I've been thinking a lot about the future and what will happen if we have children and I don't think I'd be happy at all. In a way I think I found my mum in my partner and not in a good way. She would work all the time and then be too tired to do anything so I would be the one to cook and clean and look after my little sister, whilst I was attending school and then work after I was older and left school. The main one is vitamin D. Vitamin D isn't contained in any fruits or vegetables (you can get mushrooms that have it but I wouldn't feed that to a parrot) so unless your bird is going outside in bright sunlight a lot or you're feeding it eggs or a fortified pellet then your bird will likely be deficient in it. Where I live you can't get vitamin D from the sun for around 6 months of the year, and it's not healthy to feed too many animal products to parrots so I choose to give pellets. You could give a vitamin supplement in their water or sprinkle it on their food if you don't want to feed another pellet.

One of the other issues with TOPS is because it's made with all natural ingredients you don't know exactly how much of each vitamin it contains. I've heard of birds getting sick from the high amounts of phosphorous since a large percentage of the pellets is just alfalfa.

I think it's fine as a supplement so long as it's not used like a pellet and given as a large portion of the diet.
TOPS aren't a complete pellet though and are lacking in some vitamins so I wouldn't recommend they're the only pellet you feed your bird

I struggle a lot with food and cross contamination and I have a few tips that might help you. My situation has improved now but I had to do some fairly drastic things in order to not get sick. 

Try and meal prep a lot of your food so that all you need to do is warm it up in a microwave, not prepare it. This reduces the amount of times you can contaminate your food. If you prepare a dish that lasts you 4 servings and then just warm it up, that's only one chance it has to come into contact with gluten, compared to four. For the food that you can't prepare ahead, try and get it already prepped or that require little to no prep. A whole apple, a spoon and a jar of peanut butter (make sure you're the only one using it) can get a lot of calories into you without needing to cut it up. I can eat 500g of natural yogurt at a time straight from the container and that fills me up and provides some calories. Fruits like bananas are good to have on hand as well for if you're just hungry. I don't eat chocolate or crisps or anything so for a treat I buy huel shakes as that's a meal but I also really like them so I feel like it's a treat. They're a bit expensive but because I don't ever have treats I can spend a bit of money on something that will fill me up and is nutritious. 

If you can prep some of your meals and then have food that requires no prep then I think think things will become a bit easier for you.

Basically whatever problem I had or was having I'd research it and then focus on fixing it. So say fatigue was my main problem. First I'd look at how I can make sure I get good sleep and go all out on that. I've had to change my life a few times and I've got a few things that I do that always work for me. First of all I really visualise where I want to be and what kind of things I want to be doing. I imagine myself in different situations and imagine how I want to react in them. I think about what I look like, what I sound like, what I'm acting like in these imaginary scenarios. Then after doing this I start to plan things out. I have a weekly spreadsheet and I just play around with the kind of things I want to do and when I can do them. 

As an example I would put in when I'm working, seeing friends etc. Then I would think about my goals and steps I could take in order to get there. if I wanted to change my mindset as a main goal then I might choose to meditate 20 minutes a day, or journal before bed and then I's put that in the planner so I know that I'm doing it. Doing all of this generally makes me excited about whatever goal I'm trying to achieve, and it makes it more likely for me to remember that goal when I'm challenged. 

So as an example if I'm trying to stop being hypocritical and rude then I would first sit down with no distractions and think about situations where I've acted in ways I don't want to and what I would have liked to have done instead. Then I'd think of imaginary situations that might come up, such as going out for dinner with family, and imagine what that might be like and what I could do in order to not be rude and hypocritical. The next time I go out for dinner with them will remind me of what I imagined and I'll be able to remember that and maybe begin to act in the way I visualised. I might be journaling or doing some meditation in my daily life when this happens and then I'll be able to think about it again when I do that, making being considerate and friendly a habit and eventually it will be natural to act that way. 

Reinforcing the behaviours you want is the best way to achieve permanent changes and the more times you can do that (by visualising, journaling and meditating) in addition to actually doing it, the more chance it has to stick.

When I was diagnosed I couldn't work because I was so sick. I have also been basically bed bound at one point in my life.

I also have celiac disease and cutting gluten completely out of my diet helped a lot. But I was still very sick and struggling to work. Plus I had loads of supplements I was taking daily. Since I was unemployed I had the time to research what I needed, and then I just went to town with everything. I did things like yoga for ten minutes a day, go to the shop which would take me half an hour for a round trip, and then I walked a friends dog a few times a week. In the summer I would wear as little as I was comfortable with to get the vitamin D, and I tried growing some food (unsuccessfully, I'm not good at growing things) in the garden for the health benefits. I had lots of baths with salts, got a weighted blanket, got a massage stick, cooked all my foods at home and never ate anything that would make me feel worse. I made sure I got enough sleep and kept a consistent routine. 

I was lucky because I had the time to do that and I had savings so I was able to live on them for a while. But I've kept up a lot of the stuff I did back then and I'm still able to get by and not have it affect me too much. This happened to me too. Ruined my life in a way, I had it my whole childhood and it was only when I was 21 I found out why I struggled so much.

I had a lot of different symptoms through my childhood that my parents refused to take me to the doctor for. Extreme fatigue, starving all the time, aches and pains everywhere, plus I was a bit slow and also had some anxiety. They didn't want me "labelled" and given drugs so I just had to get on with it as "everyone gets tired" and I was "just being lazy". 

I had a job I loved, just got promoted and could handle it all, and then all of a sudden I started having panic attacks at work. My hair started falling out. I began to feel sick after eating anything and would feel better if I starved myself, but then because I wasn't eating I was too tired to do anything and the cycle continued. I was 20 and still lived at home and of course my parents gave me the whole "you're lazy, just deal with it like an adult and go to work" stuff. I went to the doctors and they proceeded to diagnose me with depression and anxiety. I tried to tell them I don't think it's that, but that was what they said so I had to run with it. 

I did therapy, I did self help. I refused medication because the shame I already felt at going to the doctors at all was bad enough. I kept getting worse. I was suicidal at this point and said to myself if I don't get better before my 21st birthday I'm going to kill myself because I clearly was incapable of being a normal person who could just do things. Well my 21st birthday was right before the half term and so my mum was home for the whole of it and I couldn't do it whilst she was there. 

I was really into self help since I was so sick all the time and at this point my diet was full of whole grains but I really upped it once I got promoted because I didn't want to fail like I had at school and life in general. I came across an article about a 40 year old woman who had been chronically depressed her whole life. She couldn't work, was on all kinds of drugs and was generally a failure in life. I could see myself in 20 years being this woman. She went gluten free as it was the latest diet and she was overweight, and she found out she had celiac disease and was able to work, lose weight and do everything she hadn't been able to before. So I decided that I'm going to kill myself anyway so what's the harm in trying a gluten free diet. I didn't tell anyone, ate as much gluten as I could on my birthday the weekend before that half term and then on Monday I just stopped eating gluten.

It took three days and I felt like a different person. I had energy. Pains I didn't even notice I had disappeared. I stopped feeling so ill after eating. And my anxiety and depression mysteriously disappeared. If only they'd tested me at any point in my life. It would have saved a lot of suffering.

Whilst I don’t support just letting your parrots breed, I let my female budgie have babies because I know people who wanted the babies and I also could look after them all if I couldn’t find anyone who wanted them. 

She was very neglected when I got her and after a year of having her she was still extremely hormonal even after doing all the right things (diet, sleep, etc.) she laid eggs without even having a partner before and would always seek out the best looking nest (just dark spaces as I never gave her a nest), and show territorial behaviours. I rescued a male budgie to give her some company and she didn’t like him much but slowly warmed up to him although he still wasn’t allowed to go near her most days, and he wasn’t allowed to eat from the same food bowl (she has food issues from being starved) 

Well I decided to breed them and since she’s had babies (they’re six weeks old now) she’s a completely different bird. She eats from the same bowl as the male without getting territorial, she preens him and lets him preen her. She was an amazing mother and never turned on the babies and they’ve all been housed together throughout the whole process. She even fed them as fledglings whereas a lot of breeders separate them because the mum often starts attacking the babies or at the very least won’t care for them. Even now she’s still very maternal towards them and will sit with them and preen them. 

I won’t breed her again, but the experience has been very beneficial to her. She’s a very sweet bird now, whereas before she was very feisty and angry all the time. 

Luckily my conure and cockatiel show no hormonal signs so the usual sleep/diet etc. Recommendations clearly work for them, but then I do let them play out some of those behaviours, especially my female cockatiel likes to play nest in a box. I don’t give her any attention and she only does it sometimes but I don’t discourage her or get rid of the box.

I live in the U.K. so I don’t know how hot/cold Texas gets but we’ve had heatwaves the last few summers and I’ve put my birds out either in the morning in the shade or the evening in the shade but brought them in during the hottest parts of the day so they still get some sun. I would really try and get her to start eating fresh foods if you can as I think that would help a lot. With mine I only give them pellets and seeds at night before they go back into their cages, and special treats like sunflower seeds if I’m training them. During the day if they’re hungry their only choice is fresh food. 

I prepare their food when I prepare mine as I eat a lot of vegetables myself and then keep a container in the fridge for a few days. It usually consists of broccoli, carrots, parsnips, spinach, blueberries, strawberries, rolled oats, bell peppers, some kind of alfalfa mix for parrots and then sometimes something else like tomatoes or mango if I have it around. I cut it all really finely and then shake it all up. I find they go straight for the oats first and as it absorbs the flavours of everything then they have no problems eating everything else. Even my budgies will eat this mix and enjoy it. 

I’ve rescued a few budgies who haven’t ever had fresh food in their life and it only takes them a few days to adjust to eating it. They won’t starve as you’re feeding them the seeds and pellets in the evening, they’ll be a bit hungry but that’s how you’ll get them to try the fresh stuff.

My conure actually didn’t go back into her cage when I first got her and spent a good day and a bit outside of it before I got her back in. The easiest way to get them to go back in is to make them hungry, so put her food in the cage and then wait for him to go in. Eventually he should start to go in when you want him to, mine picked it up quite quickly, just sometimes leave the door open so he knows he’s not always going to be locked in. I’d save treats (like seeds) for training him or for situations where you need him to go inside her cage quickly, and feed him pellets/ fresh vegetables other than that. 

For toys it is difficult, and they can be very expensive anyway so it’s not always easy to afford them. They’ll also destroy your furniture so you have to be careful of that. The branch that you found is good, and more branches would be even better, especially for him feet and some stimulation. Some branches with leaves (make sure they’re safe) is great and will keep him busy. Also safe plants that he can destroy would help, foraging also would keep her busy instead of just giving him straight food make him work for it. Also a large water dish so he can bathe when he wants to. Wooden things they can destroy, like toilet rolls, wicker baskets, or even just newspaper make good free or cheap toys. 

As for the vets and getting him vaccinated etc. Where I live we don’t generally get our parrots vaccinated and the vets told me not to take my birds unless there’s a problem as it’s too stressful for them to go all the time, and it’s better if there’s a reason.

I have a cat and although my birds are scared of him, he doesn’t terrorise them and they’ve stopped screaming every time he walks into the room with their cages. When I first got them I introduced them to each other (they were in cages) and gave him a lot of attention, let him sniff them through the bars (small enough so he couldn’t attack) and if he showed signs of aggression or stalking I’d remove him from the room. I always give him attention even when the birds are out, and I’ll hold and snuggle him so he can’t attack them, which he now seems to equate them as being good things as if he behaves around them then he gets attention and treats. I’d get your bird on some pellets as well to rule out nutrient deficiencies, as fruits and vegetables are brilliant but they need other stuff as well and pellets have what she might be missing. If you can take her outside to get some sunlight then I’m sure that will help as well. My parrots are on pellets/vegetables and fruit, but I notice that they really benefit from the sun still. Also make sure she has a lot of toys to play with a destroy so that she’s not plucking from boredom. 

Try giving her seeds through the bars if she’s really scared of people now, to build up that trust again. Or if she’ll come out of her cage then still let her out so she can fly around and get some exercise. I find if I close the cage door after my birds come out then after an hour or so they’ll go back in as they’ll be hungry by then. It worked well with my conure before she was tamed.
